items.label: Onto Innovation Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: SILICON PHOTONICS called out as a new growth inflection: Onto has receiv

set.signal: SILICON PHOTONICS called out as a new growth inflection (CEO Michael Plisinski): 'Although a nascent market', Onto has received OVER $50 MILLION IN ORDERS to support it, with roughly TWO-THIRDS to be delivered in 2027, and estimates its served addressable market in silicon photonics grows to OVER $500 MILLION BY 2030. The opportunity spans light guides, light generation and detection; the products in play are Dragonfly INSPECTION (which has some metrology built into it and is where most of the traction sits) plus IRIS FILMS for more precise films / front-end metrology, with a 'fairly linear ramp of the process control technology with the volume' expected as the market scales. Silicon photonics sits in the SPECIALTY segment, which is 'more flat versus the down we originally expected at the start of the year', 'probably helped by the silicon photonics'; silicon photonics is a potential for some incremental adds next year. As heterogeneous packaging includes more die such as silicon photonics, package sizes are getting larger, which favors panel-level packaging.

items.reason: Hedge restored: the CEO said Specialty was 'probably helped' by silicon photonics, not that silicon photonics lifted it; 'nascent market' kept.
items.evidence: We're definitely seeing kind of a little bit better on the Specialty, probably helped by the silicon photonics, where it's more flat versus the down we originally expected at the start of the year.

items.label: Onto Innovation Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Driver is new-product adoption rather than process-control intensity: th

set.signal: Driver of the advanced-nodes outgrowth, per CEO Michael Plisinski: not a memory skew ('I don't think it's because we're more memory skewed') but 'us adding new products, getting those new products adopted and growing' (Iris films, integrated metrology), expanding wallet share for every dollar tied to a 10,000 wafer-start expansion. The ATLAS G6 is being used for TRANSISTOR METROLOGY AT SEVERAL NODES BELOW 2 nm, where its smaller spot size and tighter precision let customers apply OCD to parts of the wafer where they had to use test structures in the streets. Iris films and integrated metrology are both on track for RECORD 2026 revenue, with new logic applications for integrated metrology called share gain ('A year ago, we wouldn't have had hardly any, maybe zero logic for integrated metrology'). Iris G2: several shipments made, in the normal installation / qualification / performance-testing process that generally lasts 6 to 12 months; the Dragonfly G5 for FRONT-END applications has some units delivered and is running samples against the incumbent, with bigger contributions expected in 2027. New FAST-technology applications aim to predict device performance earlier in the fabrication process.

items.reason: The CEO contrasted new-product adoption with a memory skew; 'process-control intensity' was the analyst's framing (Shane Brett).
items.evidence: I don't think it's because we're more memory skewed.

set.signal: RECORD BACKLOG SURPASSING $1.1 BILLION. Mix (CEO Michael Plisinski): 'Probably 60%-70% of it is tied to this year, but 30%-40% is covering 2027, and it's still early'. The CEO frames it as customers 'confidently issuing purchase orders well in advance of the historical norms' to secure supply slots for their ramp plans. Visibility improved MOST in advanced packaging - historically the weaker-visibility segment versus advanced nodes - because demand is driven more by AI hyperscale demand than consumer demand; well over half the business tends to be from advanced packaging. Onto is starting to discuss Volume Purchase Agreements (VPAs) for 2027, which will further add to visibility.

items.reason: 'roughly double the ~$0.5B last disclosed in Q4' is the analyst's statement (Edward Yang), not confirmed by management; the CEO's 'Probably' hedge restored.
items.evidence: Correct me if I'm wrong, the last time you mentioned backlog was in fourth quarter, and at that time, it had doubled to about half a billion.

items.label: Onto Innovation Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capacity and balance sheet: NOT capacity constrained - in-house factorie

set.signal: Capacity and balance sheet: NOT capacity constrained (CEO Michael Plisinski) - in-house factories have capacity for $2 billion of revenue and the Asian EXTENDED FACTORIES have now added essentially the equal capability, reducing cycle times and adding second shifts with the capability of third shifts. The extended-factory model also cut freight and labor cost and lowered capital expenditure, a large driver of the 2026 margin expansion. 'Supply chain constraints, that's always a concern': Onto is working closely with its supply chains and 'leveraging our balance sheet a little bit'; CFO Brian Roberts: Onto is in a cycle of increasing inventory to ensure continuity of supply chain and support the revenue acceleration. Nearly $1.9B of cash and short-term investments as of June 30; $62M cash from operations in Q2, slightly over 100% of Q2 net income.

items.reason: Financing terms (convertible offering, net proceeds, buyback, capped call) and the analyst-day date (event schedule) are not captured.
items.evidence: In May, we completed a $1.5 billion 0% interest convertible debt offering maturing in 2031, which generated about $1.2 billion in net cash to the company.
